sanskrit: saptaitaṃ sapta ṛṣayaḥ śalyakartā dvādaśa | āviddhaṃ śalyaṃ cākratur indrarāśiṃ mahodaram ||
english: Seven it is, seven ṛṣis, the thorn-makers twelve — they fashioned the piercing thorn that is the Indra-heap, the great-bellied one.

sanskrit: indrarāśiṃ mitrāvaruṇāv āviddhaṃ nir akṛntatam | prasūtam indreṇogreṇa brāhmaṇānām asat pituḥ ||
english: Mitra and Varuṇa cut out the Indra-heap, that which had been pierced within; it was brought forth by fierce Indra, from one who is no fit father for brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: nainam aśnīyād abrāhmaṇo na gṛhān pra haret svān | tṛṣṭaṃ viṣam iva taimātam indrarāśiḥ khale śaye ||
english: No non-brāhmaṇa should eat of it, nor should he carry it away to his own home; bitter as the taimāta poison, the Indra-heap lies upon the threshing-floor.

sanskrit: ayaṃ śaye tanvaṃ rakṣamāṇo yo aśnāty avicakṣāṇa etam | madhye khalasya nirmita indrarāśir mahodaraḥ ||
english: This one lies here protecting its own body — whosoever eats of it heedlessly — the great-bellied Indra-heap, fashioned in the midst of the threshing-floor.

sanskrit: utaiṣa yakṣmaṃ bhavati- -indrarāśir mahodaraḥ | bhīmo annasya saṃkāśe aśva ivātti śinī naḍam ||
english: And this one too becomes a disease — the Indra-heap, the great-bellied — terrible in the semblance of food; like a horse it devours the reeds of the marshland.

sanskrit: ya indrarāśiṃ nirvapād vardhayāt khalamānyāḥ | sphātiṃ ca khalyāṃ gṛhṇātu gavāṃ ca bahu puṣyatu ||
english: He who winnows and augments the Indra-heap, the pride of the threshing-floor — may he obtain the abundance of the floor and may his cattle flourish greatly.

sanskrit: yam uvāha śunaḥśepo yam indro brahmaṇaspatiḥ | taṃ cakruḥ śivam asmabhyaṃ ṛṣayo jīvanāya kam ||
english: That which Śunaḥśepa carried, that which Indra and Bṛhaspati carried — that the ṛṣis have made auspicious for us, a pleasant thing for our living.

sanskrit: tṛḍhaṃ śākaṃ tam aśayad dattam āsīc chvāpadam | pandrā sma rupyantaḥ śere ya ādanvahutaṃ haviḥ ||
english: He set it down as an impaled plant; the offering to the dog-demon had been given. Fifteen lay suffering, those who ate the oblation that had been offered improperly.

sanskrit: anaḍuhāṃ pṛśniśaphānāṃ vahatāṃ vaharāpiṇām | kīnāśasya śramāt svedād indrarāśir ajāyata ||
english: From the sweat and toil of the ploughman, from the draught-oxen with dappled hooves, from those that draw and those that bear burdens — the Indra-heap was born.

sanskrit: yat kināśasya sveda eti saṃtaptas tanvas pari | apāṃ gāva iva tṛṣyantīr indrarāśiṃ so aśnute ||
english: When the ploughman's sweat flows from his scorched body all around — as cows thirst for water, so he consumes the Indra-heap.

sanskrit: yat kīnāśaṃ sīrapatir daṇḍena hanti manyutaḥ | yat kiṃ ca khalyaṃ sādānvavam indrarāśau tad āhitam ||
english: Whatever the lord of the plough strikes with the rod in his anger at the ploughman, and whatever of the threshing-floor pertaining to the perennial horse-offering — all that is deposited in the Indra-heap.

sanskrit: ulūkhalamusalaṃ tāni codaya sūrpaṃ nāry apavice kṛṇuṣva | vāhāya putrāya gotama indrarāśiṃ madhumantaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: Rouse those, the mortar and pestle; O woman, make the winnowing-fan for the fanning. May Gotama make the sweet Indra-heap ready for his son, the bearer.

sanskrit: etat sūrpaṃ jaritar ā hara- -ulūkhalamusalaṃ kumbhy ā gahi | putrā no adya sudinatve ahni pittam aśnanta madhumantam aṃśum ||
english: O singer of praise, bring this winnowing-fan hither; come, O pot, to the mortar and pestle. May our sons today, on this day of fair brightness, eat the sweet sap, the portion of the father.

sanskrit: agnir no dūtaḥ prahito 'yam āgan sa naḥ sarvam annam aviṣaṃ kṛṇotu | nirāviddham akṛtaṃ brahmaṇeto 'domadhaṃ pittam atta prasūtāḥ ||
english: Agni has come here, dispatched as our messenger; may he render all our food free from poison. That which is unpierced and unprocessed — from this brāhmaṇa here — eat, ye who are born, the intoxicating portion of the father.

sanskrit: svādo pito madho pita upa naḥ pitav ā gahi | śivaḥ śivābhir ūtibhiḥ ||
english: O sweet food, O honey-food, come unto us for our nourishment, O food; auspicious, with auspicious protections.

sanskrit: siṃho bhūtvā gā mṛṇāty agnir bhūtvā dhānyam | indrarāśir anirmito mayāraṃ cāva gacchati ||
english: Having become a lion, it crushes the cattle; having become fire, it consumes the grain. The Indra-heap, when unpropitiated, goes down along with the peacock.

sanskrit: śatakāṇḍo duścyavanaḥ sahasraparṇa uttiraḥ | darbho ya ugra oṣadhis taṃ te badhnāmy āyuṣe ||
english: The hundred-stemmed, the unshakeable, the thousand-leafed, the lofty — darbha, the fierce herb: I bind you with it for long life.

sanskrit: nāsya keśān pra vapanti norasi tāḍam ā ghnate | yasmā acchinnaparṇena darbheṇa śarma yacchati ||
english: They do not shave his hair, nor do they strike a blow upon his chest — to him to whom shelter is granted with the uncut-leafed darbha.

sanskrit: divi te tūlam oṣadhe pṛthivyām asi niṣṭhitaḥ | tvayā sahasrakāṇḍena āyuṣ pra vardhayāmahe ||
english: In heaven is your tuft, O herb; upon the earth you are firmly established. By you, O thousand-stemmed one, we cause long life to increase.

sanskrit: tisro divo aty atṛṇas tisra imāḥ pṛthivīr uta | tayāhaṃ sarvān durhārdo jihvāṃ ni tṛṇadmi vacāṃsi ca ||
english: The three heavens you pierced through, and these three earths likewise. With it I cut off the tongue and the speech of all the ill-willed.

sanskrit: tvam asi sahamāno aham asmi sahasvān | ubhau sahasvantau bhūtvā sapatnān sahiṣīvahi ||
english: You are the overpowering one; I am the possessor of overpowering strength. Both of us, having become mighty, let us overcome the rivals.

sanskrit: sahasva no abhimātiṃ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | sahasva sarvān durhārdaḥ suhārdo me bahūn kṛdhi ||
english: Overpower the malice against us; overpower the one who marches in battle-array. Overpower all the ill-willed; make my well-wishers many.

sanskrit: darbheṇa devajātena diviṣṭambhena śaśvad it | tenāhaṃ sasvato janām̐ asanaṃ sanavāni ca ||
english: With the darbha born of the gods, the perpetual pillar of heaven — with it I shall win people forever and shall obtain boons.

sanskrit: priyaṃ mā darbhaṃ kṛṇu brahmarājanyābhyāṃ śūdrāya cāryāya ca | yasmai ca kāmayāmahe sarvasmai ca vipaśyate ||
english: Make me dear through the darbha to the brāhmaṇa and the rājanya, to the śūdra and the ārya, to whomsoever we wish, and to every far-sighted one.

sanskrit: yo jāyamānaḥ pṛthivīm adṛṃhad yo astabhnād antarikṣaṃ divaṃ ca | yaṃ bibhrataṃ nanu pāpmā viveda sa no 'yaṃ darbho dharuṇo divā kaḥ ||
english: He who at his birth made the earth firm, who propped up the atmosphere and heaven — the evil has never known him as he is borne: may this darbha be a sustainer, a shining one for us.

sanskrit: sapatnahā śatakāṇḍaḥ sahasvān oṣadhīnāṃ prathamaḥ saṃ babhūva | sa no 'yaṃ darbhaḥ pari pātu viśvatas tena sākṣīya pṛtanāḥ pṛtanyataḥ ||
english: The hundred-stemmed, the rival-slayer, the mighty — first among herbs it came into being. May this darbha guard us on all sides; with it may I overcome the battle-lines of those who battle against us.
